'''''Micranthes stellaris''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Saxifraga stellaris''''', the '''starry saxifrage''' or '''hairy kidney-wort''', is an [[Arctic–alpine]] species in the family [[Saxifragaceae]].<ref name=POWO_77068348-1>{{citation |mode=cs1 |title=''Micranthes stellaris'' (L.) Galasso, Banfi & Soldano |work=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77068348-1 |access-date=2022-11-20}}</ref><ref name="FischAdler">{{cite book |author=Manfred A. Fischer, Wolfgang Adler & Karl Oswald |year=2005 |title=Exkursionsflora für Österreich, Liechtenstein und Südtirol |publisher=Oberösterreichische Landesmuseen |location=Linz |isbn=978-3-85474-140-4 |chapter=Steinbrechblütige / ''Saxifraganae'' |language=de |page=397}}</ref> It produces panicles of 5–10 white flowers on a stem up to {{convert|20|cm|abbr=on}} tall, rising from a basal leaf rosette. One subspecies is found from eastern Canada to Russia, including the British Isles, while another is found in the mountains of southern Europe.

==Description==
[[File:Saxifraga stellaris closeup.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.86|Close-up of a flower, showing the two yellow spots at the base of each petal]]
''Micranthes stellaris'' grows as a [[Rosette (botany)|leaf rosette]], which produces a generally leafless stem up to {{convert|20|cm}} tall.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book |author=Clive A. Stace |author-link=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |url=https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac |url-access=limited |edition=3rd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |location=Cambridge |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 |page=[https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac/page/n165 130]}}</ref> The leaves are toothed and somewhat fleshy, ovate or obovate, and without an obvious [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]].<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref name="Pardoe">{{cite book |author=Heather Pardoe |year=1995 |title=Mountain Plants of the British Isles |series=British Plant Life |volume=4 |publisher=[[National Museums and Galleries of Wales]] |location=Cardiff |isbn=978-0-7200-0423-6 |page=44}}</ref> They are typically {{convert|3|cm|abbr=on}} long (varying from {{convert|1|to|5|cm|1|disp=or}}), with a cuneate (wedge-shaped) base.<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref name="FNA"/><ref name="M&M">{{cite book |editor=James Ferguson-Lees & Bruce Campbell |year=1978 |title=Mountains and Moorlands |series=The Natural History of Britain and Northern Europe |publisher=George Rainbird |isbn=978-0-340-22615-5 |page=104}}</ref>

The flowers are borne in a loose [[panicle]] comprising 5–10 flowers;<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref name="Stace"/> each flower has deflexed [[sepal]]s, surrounding five white [[petal]]s, {{convert|3|-|6|mm}} long, with two yellow or red spots near the base.<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref name="Stace"/> There are 10 stamens. The [[anther]]s are also red or yellow.<ref name="Pardoe"/> Flowers are borne from June to August.<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref name="Pardoe"/>

The seeds are dark brown, glabrous, {{convert|0.6|-|0.8|mm|abbr=on}} long, and {{convert|0.3|-|0.4|mm|abbr=on}} wide. They are elliptic, ovoid or reniform in shape, with longitudinal ribs bearing spines.<ref name="seeds">{{cite book |author=Vít Bojňanský & Agáta Fargašová |year=2007 |title=Atlas of Seeds and Fruits of Central and East-European Flora: The Carpathian Mountains Region |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |isbn=978-1-4020-5361-0 |page=239 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QSMe0qHGVaAC&pg=PA239}}</ref> ''M. stellaris'' has a [[chromosome number]] of 2''n'' = 28.<ref name="Stace"/><ref name="FNA"/><ref name="seeds"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Micranthes stellaris'' was [[species description|first described]] by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his 1753 work ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' as ''Saxifraga stellaris''.<ref name=POWO_77068348-1/><ref name="Vargas"/><ref name="SP">{{cite book |author=Carolus Linnaeus |author-link=Carl Linnaeus |year=1753 |title=[[Species Plantarum]] |language=la |chapter=[''Saxifraga''] ''stellaris'' |volume=1 |page=400 |chapter-url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358106#page/412/mode/1up |publisher=Laurentius Salvius |location=Stockholm}}</ref> Linnaeus noted the species' occurrence in the mountains of [[Spitsbergen]], [[Sápmi|Lapland]], [[Switzerland]], [[Styria]] and [[Westmorland]].<ref name="SP"/> The [[nominate subspecies]], ''Micranthes stellaris'' subsp. ''stellaris'' is the northern subspecies, occurring from Canada to Russia, including the British Isles.<ref name="Vargas"/> The subspecies in the [[Alpide belt]] and other mountains in southern Europe is often called ''M. stellaris'' subsp. ''alpigena'', but an older name has [[Principle of Priority|priority]] – ''M. stellaris'' subsp. ''robusta''.<ref name="Vargas">{{cite book |author=Pablo Vargas |year=2003 |chapter=''Saxifraga'' L. |series=Flora Ibérica |title=Ebenaceae–Saxifragaceae |volume=5 |edition=2nd |isbn=978-84-00-07641-2 |publisher=[[Spanish National Research Council|Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas]] |pages=170–171 |language=es}}</ref> The name ''M. stellaris'' subsp. ''prolifera'' is used for plants from the [[Southern Limestone Alps|south-eastern Alps]] which have few flowers but produce [[bulbils]] along the stems.<ref name="FischAdler"/><ref>{{cite thesis |author=Eva Schönbeck-Temesy |author-link=Eva Schönbeck-Temesy |year=1954 |degree=Ph.D. |id=[[Sub auspiciis Praesidentis]] |publisher=[[University of Graz]] |title=Der Formenkreis von ''Saxifraga stellaris'' Linné |trans-title=The polytypic species ''Saxifraga stellaris'' Linné}}</ref>

==Distribution and ecology==
[[File:Saxifraga stellaris habitat.jpg|thumb|left|Typical habitat: on wet rocks in a wet mountain flush]]
''Micranthes stellaris'' has an [[Arctic–alpine|Arctic–alpine distribution]].<ref name="FischAdler"/> It is found from [[Baffin Island]], [[Labrador]] and [[Greenland]] to Arctic [[Russia]], including [[Iceland]], [[Scandinavia]] and the [[British Isles]].<ref name="Pardoe"/><ref name="FNA">{{cite book |author=Luc Brouillet & Patrick E. Elvander |year=2009 |chapter=''Micranthes stellaris'' (Linnaeus) Galasso, Banfi & Soldano, Atti Soc. Ital. Sci. Nat. Mus. Civico Storia Nat. Milano. 146: 231. 2005 |page=57 |series=[[Flora of North America]] |volume=8 |title=Magnoliophyta: Paeoniaceae to Ericaceae |isbn=978-0-19-534026-6 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |chapter-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250065880}}</ref> Further south, it is found from the [[Sierra Nevada (Spain)|Sierra Nevada]] in southern Spain to the eastern Carpathians,<ref name="seeds"/><ref name="Vargas"/> including lower ranges such as the [[Massif Central]].<ref name="Kropf">{{cite journal |author=Matthias Kropf, Hans P. Comes & Joachim W. Kadereit |year=2008 |title=Causes of the genetic architecture of south-west European high mountain disjuncts |journal=[[Plant Ecology & Diversity]] |volume=1 |issue=2 <!--|work=History, evolution and future of arctic and alpine flora -->|pages=217–228 |doi=10.1080/17550870802331938|s2cid=84638877 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In the Arctic, ''M. stellaris'' may occur down to sea level. Within the British Isles, ''M. stellaris''  is abundant in [[North Wales]], [[Northern England]] and [[Scotland]], reaching the summit of [[Ben Nevis]] ({{convert|1344|m|disp=or|abbr=on}}), but is only found locally in [[Ireland]].<ref name="Stace"/><ref name="Pardoe"/><ref name="NewAtlas"/> Its southernmost stations in [[Great Britain]] are the slopes of [[Plynlimon]] and the [[River Rheidol|Rheidol valley]]; it does not occur in the mountains of [[South Wales]].<ref>{{cite book |author=J. L. Davies & D. P. Kirby |year=1994 |title=Cardiganshire County History: from the Earliest Times to the Coming of the Normans |volume= 1 |series=Cardiganshire County History |publisher=[[University of Wales Press]] |isbn=978-0-7083-1170-7 |page=74}}</ref> In the [[Vosges Mountains|Vosges]], it occurs around {{convert|3600|ft|abbr=on}}, but only rarely below {{convert|4300|-|4600|ft|abbr=on}} in the [[Swiss Alps]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Arthur Henfrey |author-link=Arthur Henfrey (botanist) |year=1977 |orig-year=1852 |title=The Vegetation of Europe |publisher=J. Van Voorst |location=London |series=Outlines of the Natural History of Europe |volume=1 |isbn=978-0-405-10397-1 |page=225 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oxyDMJiKhHAC&pg=PA225}}</ref> In the [[Sierra Nevada (Spain)|Sierra Nevada]] of southern Spain, it lives at up to {{convert|3350|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name="Kropf"/>

''Micranthes stellaris'' lives in damp environments, such as wet flushes, beside streams or springs, or on wet rock ledges.<ref name="FNA"/><ref name="M&M"/><ref name="NewAtlas">{{cite book |author=Christopher David Preston, D. Pearman & Trevor D. Dines |year=2002 |title=New Atlas of the British & Irish Flora: an Atlas of the Vascular Plants of Britain, Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands |volume=1 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-851067-3 |chapter=''Saxifraga stellaris'' (starry saxifrage) |chapter-url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/saxifraga-stellaris}}</ref> It is [[self-compatible]], but its flowers are [[protandry|protandrous]], and are usually [[pollination|pollinated]] by [[fly|flies]].<ref name="Kropf"/>
